project.name: Periodic KYC refresh programme
project.description: A bank must refresh KYC for existing customers on the regulator's schedule. Requirements are firm, regulated and unlikely to change. Good for showing a plan-driven recommendation (V-Model or Waterfall).

documents.title: 01 Policy Extract
documents.masked_text:
Board-approved KYC Refresh Policy, version 3.1 (final, approved)

1. Customers rated high risk must have their KYC information updated at least every 2 years, medium risk every 8 years and low risk every 10 years.
2. The bank must notify each customer at least 30 days before the due date by SMS and email, and again at 7 days.
3. Customers may confirm that their details are unchanged through a self-declaration in the mobile app or net banking, without visiting a branch.
4. Where the address has changed, a proof of the new address must be collected and verified.
5. Updated KYC records must be uploaded to the Central KYC Records Registry within 10 days.
6. Accounts must not be frozen for a missing update until two reminders have been sent and 30 days have passed after the due date. Every freeze must be approved by a branch manager and recorded.
7. All KYC records and refresh evidence must be retained for at least 5 years after the relationship ends and be retrievable within 24 hours for an auditor.
8. Customer identifiers must be encrypted at rest and masked on every screen except for authorised compliance staff.

documents.title: 02 Business Requirements
documents.masked_text:
Business requirements document (final), KYC Refresh Programme, owner: Meera Shah (Business Analyst)

The programme covers all 2.4 million existing retail customers over 24 months. Scope, policy and the regulator's schedule are fixed and have been signed off by the steering committee.

BR-1: The system shall calculate each customer's next KYC due date from the risk category.
BR-2: The system shall send reminders at 30 days and 7 days before the due date.
BR-3: The system shall let a customer submit a self-declaration through the mobile app and net banking.
BR-4: The system shall support address-change proof upload and verification by an operations officer within 2 business days.
BR-5: The system shall submit refreshed records to the central KYC registry within 10 days.
BR-6: The system shall record every account freeze together with the approving branch manager.
BR-7: The system shall produce a monthly compliance report of due, completed and overdue refreshes.
The existing core banking and CRM platforms remain unchanged and are accessed through the approved integration layer.

controls.title: Customer identification and verification
controls.description: Regulated entities must identify every customer before establishing an account-based relationship and verify identity using an Officially Valid Document (passport, driving licence, voter ID, proof of Aadhaar possession, NREGA card) or its equivalent e-document, together with PAN or Form 60. Customers must not be allowed to open anonymous or fictitious-name accounts.

controls.title: Risk-based customer categorisation
controls.description: Each customer must be categorised as low, medium or high risk using documented parameters such as customer type, geography, product, delivery channel and transaction pattern. The intensity of due diligence and monitoring must match the assigned risk category, and the categorisation must be reviewable.

controls.title: Sanctions and watchlist screening
controls.description: Customers and related parties must be screened against applicable sanctions lists, and assets of designated persons must be frozen without delay and reported to the authorities.

controls.title: PEP identification and senior approval
controls.description: Institutions need risk-management systems to determine whether a customer or beneficial owner is a politically exposed person and, for foreign PEPs and higher-risk domestic PEPs, must obtain senior management approval, establish source of wealth and funds, and conduct enhanced ongoing monitoring.

controls.title: Beneficial ownership of legal entities
controls.description: For companies, partnerships, trusts and other legal entities, the natural persons who ultimately own or control the entity must be identified and verified. A controlling ownership interest is defined by a percentage threshold set in the direction (verify the current figure); where no owner meets the threshold the person exercising control, or the senior managing official, is identified.

controls.title: Enhanced due diligence for high-risk customers
controls.description: High-risk customers, politically exposed persons and non-face-to-face customers require enhanced due diligence: additional identity evidence, source of funds or wealth where relevant, senior management approval before establishing or continuing a relationship with a PEP, and closer ongoing monitoring.

controls.title: Notice and consent for personal data
controls.description: Personal data may be processed only for a lawful purpose, with free, specific, informed and unambiguous consent after a clear notice, or under a defined legitimate use such as compliance with a legal obligation. Consent must be as easy to withdraw as to give, and the data fiduciary must be able to show it was obtained.

controls.title: Data minimisation and purpose limitation
controls.description: Only the personal data necessary for the stated purpose may be collected, and it must be erased once the purpose is served unless a law requires retention. KYC records retained under anti-money-laundering law are a legal-retention case.
controls.suggested_requirement: The system shall collect only the identity data necessary for KYC and shall not reuse it for other purposes without separate consent.

controls.title: Record retention for at least five years
controls.description: Identification records and transaction records must be preserved for at least five years after the business relationship ends or the transaction takes place, in a form that can be produced promptly for competent authorities.

controls.title: Periodic KYC refresh (re-KYC)
controls.description: KYC information must be periodically updated: at least every two years for high-risk customers, every eight years for medium-risk and every ten years for low-risk customers. Customers must be able to submit self-declarations of unchanged details, and accounts must not be closed without notice for missing updates.

controls.title: Ongoing transaction monitoring
controls.description: Transactions must be monitored on an ongoing basis against the customer's profile and risk category, with alert rules calibrated to risk, documented alert handling, and prescribed threshold reports such as large cash transactions.
controls.suggested_requirement: The system shall monitor customer transactions against their risk profile and raise documented alerts for unusual activity.

controls.title: Suspicious activity reporting
controls.description: Reporting entities must report suspicious transactions to the Financial Intelligence Unit - India promptly after concluding that a transaction is suspicious (the Rules set a short working-day deadline, verify the current figure), must not tip off the customer, and must keep the reasoning for decisions not to report.

controls.title: Biometric liveness and presentation-attack detection
controls.description: Biometric capture used for identity verification should include presentation attack detection (liveness) that is tested against spoofing with photos, replayed video, masks and deepfakes, and report attack-detection error rates.

controls.title: Document authenticity and tamper detection
controls.description: Identity assurance level 2 requires evidence of identity to be validated as genuine and the applicant to be verified as its owner, in person or remotely, using biometric comparison or equivalent, with detection of forged or tampered documents and presentation attacks.

controls.title: Central KYC registry integration
controls.description: Regulated entities must upload customer KYC records to the Central KYC Records Registry (CKYCR) within the prescribed period after onboarding, generate or use the KYC identifier, and fetch existing records from the registry before asking the customer to resubmit documents.

controls.title: Tamper-evident audit trail of KYC decisions
controls.description: Identification records and transaction records must be preserved for at least five years after the business relationship ends or the transaction takes place, in a form that can be produced promptly for competent authorities.

controls.title: Encryption and masking of KYC data
controls.description: The data fiduciary must protect personal data in its possession or under its control, including data processed by processors, by taking reasonable security safeguards such as encryption, obfuscation or masking, access controls and logging, to prevent a personal data breach.

controls.title: Role-based access to KYC data
controls.description: An information security management system should apply controls for access management and least privilege, cryptography, logging and monitoring, secure development, supplier relationships and incident management.
controls.suggested_requirement: The system shall restrict access to KYC records by role on a least-privilege basis and log every access to full identity documents.

controls.title: Breach detection and notification
controls.description: On a personal data breach the data fiduciary must notify the Data Protection Board and each affected data principal in the prescribed form and manner.

controls.title: Data-subject rights handling
controls.description: Data principals have the right to access a summary of their data and processing, to correct and complete it, to request erasure (subject to legal retention), to grievance redress, and to nominate another person to exercise rights.

controls.title: Manual review and appeal of automated decisions
controls.description: People have the right not to be subject to solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects, such as automatically rejecting an account application. Where such decisions are permitted, safeguards include the right to human intervention, to express a view and to contest the decision.

threats.threat: Deepfake or synthetic media used to bypass liveness detection during remote onboarding.
Modification of KYC records or evidence in the database by an unauthorized internal user.
A branch manager denies approving an account freeze despite the action being taken.
Unauthorized access to full identity documents by staff members without a legitimate business need.
Flooding the self-declaration endpoint to prevent legitimate customers from updating their KYC status.
A standard user exploits the integration layer to gain administrative access to the core banking system.
Forged identity documents submitted during onboarding that pass initial automated checks.
Leaking of customer PII during the transmission to the Central KYC Records Registry.

risks.risk: Failure to trigger re-KYC for high-risk customers leads to regulatory non-compliance and increased exposure to money laundering.
risks.mitigation: Implement an automated scheduler that flags accounts based on risk profile and last KYC date.

risks.risk: Outdated KYC data for medium-risk customers may result in regulatory fines and inability to contact customers for fraud prevention.
risks.mitigation: Automate periodic review cycles integrated with the core banking system.

risks.risk: Long refresh intervals for low-risk customers could lead to stale data, hindering effective risk monitoring.
risks.mitigation: Establish a centralized data refresh dashboard for monitoring compliance status.

risks.risk: Missing the 30-day notification window results in poor customer experience and higher rates of account non-compliance.
risks.mitigation: Implement a robust notification engine with delivery receipts.

risks.risk: Failure to send the 7-day reminder increases the likelihood of account freezes, causing customer churn and support overhead.
risks.mitigation: Automate multi-channel notification triggers.

risks.risk: Lack of a self-declaration feature forces manual branch visits, increasing operational costs and customer friction.
risks.mitigation: Prioritize development of the self-declaration module in the mobile app.

risks.risk: Vague verification standards for address changes may lead to fraudulent address updates and identity theft.
risks.mitigation: Define a strict list of acceptable proof-of-address documents and verification workflows.

risks.risk: Ambiguity in the CKYCR upload process risks regulatory penalties for delayed or incorrect reporting.
risks.mitigation: Define clear technical specifications for CKYCR API integration and error handling.

risks.risk: Incorrect implementation of the freeze logic could lead to wrongful account suspension, causing legal and reputational damage.
risks.mitigation: Implement a state-machine based logic for account status transitions.

risks.risk: Unauthorized account freezes could occur if the approval workflow is bypassed or not properly enforced.
risks.mitigation: Enforce mandatory digital signatures or MFA for manager approvals.

risks.risk: Failure to retain records for the required period leads to inability to respond to legal requests or audits.
risks.mitigation: Implement automated data archival policies.

risks.risk: Inability to retrieve records within 24 hours results in audit failure and regulatory sanctions.
risks.mitigation: Implement an indexed document management system with high availability.

risks.risk: Unencrypted identifiers at rest expose the bank to data breaches and violation of privacy laws.
risks.mitigation: Implement AES-256 encryption for all PII at rest.

risks.risk: Excessive exposure of PII to unauthorized staff increases the risk of internal data leakage.
risks.mitigation: Implement role-based access control (RBAC) and dynamic data masking.

risks.risk: Incorrect calculation of due dates leads to missed compliance deadlines and regulatory exposure.
risks.mitigation: Define explicit business rules for risk-based due date calculation.

risks.risk: Ambiguous reminder logic may result in no notifications being sent, leading to mass account freezes.
risks.mitigation: Specify exact timing and trigger conditions for notifications.

risks.risk: Lack of clear submission workflows for self-declaration leads to data integrity issues and customer frustration.
risks.mitigation: Design a structured UI flow for self-declaration submission.

risks.risk: Incomplete support for address-change uploads prevents customers from updating records, causing compliance gaps.
risks.mitigation: Define file format, size, and validation requirements for uploads.

risks.risk: Undefined verification SLAs lead to operational bottlenecks and delayed compliance updates.
risks.mitigation: Establish a queue management system with automated SLA monitoring.

risks.risk: Vague submission requirements to the central registry lead to data rejection and non-compliance.
risks.mitigation: Standardize the data mapping and validation schema for registry submissions.

risks.risk: Missing audit trails for account freezes prevent accountability and legal defense in case of disputes.
risks.mitigation: Implement immutable logging for all administrative actions.

risks.risk: Lack of reporting capabilities prevents management from identifying systemic compliance failures.
risks.mitigation: Develop a reporting module with automated compliance dashboards.

risks.risk: Unsecured or poorly defined integrations expose core banking systems to unauthorized access.
risks.mitigation: Use an API gateway with strict authentication and rate limiting.

risks.risk: Failure to screen against sanctions lists leads to severe legal penalties and involvement in illicit financial activities.
risks.mitigation: Integrate real-time sanctions screening with automated blocking.

risks.risk: Failure to identify PEPs leads to regulatory scrutiny and reputational damage.
risks.mitigation: Implement automated PEP screening and mandatory senior management approval workflows.

risks.risk: Inaccurate UBO identification facilitates money laundering through complex corporate structures.
risks.mitigation: Implement mandatory UBO data collection and verification steps.

risks.risk: Inadequate EDD for high-risk customers increases the bank's exposure to financial crime.
risks.mitigation: Automate EDD triggers and compliance review workflows.

risks.risk: Collecting data without valid consent violates privacy laws and leads to heavy fines.
risks.mitigation: Implement a mandatory consent capture step before any data collection.

risks.risk: Failure to file STRs correctly or timely leads to severe regulatory penalties and legal liability.
risks.mitigation: Provide a secure, restricted interface for STR filing.

risks.risk: Weak liveness detection allows identity spoofing, leading to fraudulent account openings.
risks.mitigation: Use certified liveness detection software.

risks.risk: Failure to detect tampered documents allows fraudsters to bypass KYC controls.
risks.mitigation: Implement automated document forensic analysis.

risks.risk: Excessive access to KYC records increases the risk of insider threats and data theft.
risks.mitigation: Enforce strict RBAC and audit all access logs.

risks.risk: Delayed breach notification leads to regulatory fines and loss of customer trust.
risks.mitigation: Establish an automated incident response and notification plan.

risks.risk: Failure to honor data rights leads to privacy law violations and legal action.
risks.mitigation: Implement a data management module that tracks retention vs. erasure requests.

risks.risk: Unencrypted documents are vulnerable to theft if the storage layer is compromised.
risks.mitigation: Implement encryption at rest for all document storage.

risks.risk: Insecure communication channels allow man-in-the-middle attacks, compromising customer data.
risks.mitigation: Enforce TLS 1.2+ and certificate pinning.

risks.risk: Lack of immutable logs allows for tampering with account freeze history, hindering investigations.
risks.mitigation: Use write-once-read-many (WORM) storage for audit logs.

risks.risk: Failure to purge data violates data minimization principles and increases liability.
risks.mitigation: Automate data lifecycle management policies.

risks.risk: Compromised staff credentials could lead to unauthorized access to the entire KYC database.
risks.mitigation: Enforce MFA for all administrative access.

risks.risk: Digital tampering of documents goes undetected, allowing fraudulent address updates.
risks.mitigation: Implement automated integrity checks on all uploads.

risks.risk: Unauthorized submission of self-declarations leads to data corruption and compliance failures.
risks.mitigation: Ensure all self-declaration endpoints require authenticated sessions.

risks.risk: Lack of rate limiting allows for automated abuse or DoS attacks on the KYC portal.
risks.mitigation: Implement rate limiting at the API gateway level.

narrative.explanation: The Waterfall model is the most suitable choice because the project requires high levels of documentation and testing (4/5) to satisfy regulatory criticality (4/5) and audit requirements. While requirement stability is currently low (5/5) due to 12 vague requirements and 4 open conflicts, the project's focus on mandatory controls and legacy system integration benefits from the structured, sequential approach of Waterfall. The runner-up, Agile-V hybrid, offers more flexibility to address the current requirement ambiguity, but Waterfall provides the necessary rigor for the 7 high-risk security requirements and the overall consequence of failure (3/5).
tradeoffs: Reduced ability to pivot quickly as requirements clarify.
Delayed discovery of integration issues with core banking systems.
Higher risk of rework if the 12 vague requirements are misinterpreted during the initial design phase.
would_change_if: If the 12 vague requirements are finalized and conflicts are resolved, the V-Model would become more attractive for its superior verification capabilities.
If the project timeline shifts to require continuous delivery, an Agile-DevSecOps hybrid would overtake Waterfall.
